name: ditaa
description: Convert ASCII diagrams into proper bitmap graphics

repo.name: ditaa
repo.description: ditaa is a small command-line utility that can convert diagrams drawn using ascii art ('drawings' that contain characters that resemble lines like | / - ), into proper bitmap graphics.

readme.summary: Strong concept explanation and syntax examples, but installation is sparse and troubleshooting is completely absent.
readme.top_issue: No troubleshooting section — common issues like Java version conflicts, rendering problems, or platform-specific setup are undocumented.

injection_risks.description: Potential command injection risk in getExternalRenderClasspath method, where user-controlled input is used to construct a classpath string.
Potential XML injection risk in parseFile method, where user-controlled input is used to construct an XML file path.

critical_findings: Potential command injection risk in getExternalRenderClasspath method
Lack of validation for properties loaded from .properties files
security.summary: The code has some security concerns, including potential command injection and XML injection risks, but overall it appears to be moderately secure.

common_complaints: No releases since 2018 despite committed bugfixes and features
Critical bugs causing crashes (IndexOutOfBounds, Sphinx errors)
Color parsing conflicts with text content (c802 treated as color)
Performance issues with complex diagrams (30+ second render times)
praise_themes: Useful and appreciated tool for ASCII-to-image diagramming
Text-based diagram syntax is valued by users
sentiment.summary: The ditaa project exhibits clear abandonment signals with stale issues dating 5+ years, no releases since 2018, multiple unresponded critical bugs, explicit user questioning of maintenance status, and an unreachable maintainer for related packages.

red_flags: Maintainer expresses demotivation and lack of time
Some responses are brief or vague
communication.summary: The maintainer is generally responsive but shows signs of reduced interest in the project, which could affect its future development.
